Stated Claim / Post Context:
Heartbreaking moment Constable Mia Lay's boyfriend talks about going wedding ring shopping with her - as her family farewell their 'beautiful girl' killed while on duty

St Andrew's Cathedral, in central Sydney, held the funeral for 20-year-old rookie cop Mia Lay on Wednesday.

Actual Article Body:
By ASHLEY NICKEL FOR DAILY MAIL and FARID FARID FOR AUSTRALIAN ASSOCIATED PRESS

Published:  19:13 AEST, 7 October 2026   |  Updated:  21:54 AEST, 7 October 2026

Donning blue and white checked ribbons, hundreds of mourners have packed a cathedral to farewell Constable Mia Lay after she was killed in a horrific crash.

The 20-year-old rookie cop had been with NSW Police for only 16 months when the patrol car she was a passenger in crashed into a tree, on September 25 in the Sydney suburb of Redfern, while en route to a job.

A flood of uniformed police officers solemnly assembled outside St Andrew's Cathedral in central Sydney on Wednesday, as her distraught parents and many dignitaries filed in, including NSW Premier Chris Minns and Police Minister Yasmin Catley.

One of the most heartbreaking stories came from Constable Lay's partner Daniel Vasquez.

He revealed the pair had gone ring shopping shortly before her death and he had intended to propose during a holiday in Fiji, planned for this month.

'Somehow she already knew and had told everyone,' Vasquez said.

'She often said to me, 'You know I'm always going to say yes so hurry up and ask me already'.

'I wish I had, Mia.'

Mia Lay's partner Daniel Vasquez (above) had gone ring shopping with the deceased policewoman shortly before she was killed in a car crash

The couple (above) met at the police academy and graduated from the same class in May 2025

Vasquez (right) had planned to propose to Const Lay during a trip to Fiji, planned for this month

Dressed in full police uniform, Vasquez recounted how they shared a connection at the police academy and graduated from the same class in May 2025.

'She put others before herself and was fiercely loyal to the people she loved,' he said.

'She was my entire world.'

A rendition of the spiritual Amazing Grace opened the sombre service for the junior constable, who was described as well-loved.

Choking back tears, Const Lay's father Clem described her as his 'first-born flower' who brought passion and lit up a room.

'My heart is completely shattered, the pain of losing her is devastating, a sudden blinding darkness has settled over me, her brothers and her sister,' he said.

'We are a family broken by her sudden absence.'

He wiped away tears as he praised her 'grit and bravery' in her young policing career.

Const Lay's father Clem (pictured together) described her as his 'first-born flower' in an emotional speech

Const Lay was killed when the patrol car she was a passenger in crashed into a tree on September 25

Hundreds of mourners solemnly assembled outside St Andrew's Cathedral in central Sydney on Wednesday for the funeral

'You were taken from us far too soon,' Mr Lay said.

'I'd give anything to hold you one more time ... our hearts are broken.'

NSW Police Commissioner Mal Lanyon paid tribute to the 'impressive, resilient and kind-hearted woman' and said she was well-loved by colleagues.

'She has left an enduring legacy which we honour here today,' he said.

'She demonstrated exceptional promise, embracing policing with enthusiasm and earned the respect of those around her.'

He listed a series of impressive achievements in her short law enforcement career, including arresting a man brandishing a rifle.

The commissioner announced Const Lay had been posthumously awarded the National Police Service Medal and the NSW Police Force Medal for Ethical and Diligence Service.

'You will not be forgotten,' Mr Lanyon said.

NSW Police Commissioner Mal Lanyon described Const Lay as an 'impressive, resilient and kind-hearted woman'

Vasquez (above) said of Const Lay: 'She was my entire world'

Many dignitaries attended, including NSW Premier Chris Minns and Police Minister Yasmin Catley

'You have left an enormous legacy which we will continue to honour.'

Her death was commemorated on National Police Remembrance Day on September 29 and was described as a dark day by Ms Catley.

In 2027, Const Lay's name will be added to the Nati
